scope: Why Mental Health chapter library only

completedMappings.title: Understanding Mental Health and Wellbeing
completedMappings.message: Wellbeing is shaped by daily life, relationships, circumstances and practical support.

completedMappings.title: Recognizing Emotions and Responding to Them
completedMappings.message: Different emotions can be acknowledged while people have space to choose safe responses.

completedMappings.title: Understanding Stress and Healthy Coping Strategies
completedMappings.message: Practical pressures call for manageable planning and assistance, not blame or guaranteed relief.

completedMappings.title: Understanding Anxiety and Anxiety Disorders
completedMappings.message: Everyday worry deserves understanding and respectful support without diagnosing from appearance.

completedMappings.title: Understanding Depression and Depressive Disorders
completedMappings.message: Quiet presence and small offers of support can respect low energy and individual circumstances.

completedMappings.title: Understanding Trauma and Post-Traumatic Stress
completedMappings.message: Safety, choice, personal space and voluntary access to support matter; no pressure to disclose.

completedMappings.title: Understanding Grief, Loss, and Emotional Adjustment
completedMappings.message: Leaving a familiar place is one form of loss; grief has no compulsory stages or universal timeline.

completedMappings.title: Understanding Sleep and Mental Wellbeing
completedMappings.message: Sleep happens within daily rhythms and real living circumstances; an evening routine is an option, not a guaranteed solution.

completedMappings.title: Relationships, Social Connection, and Mental Wellbeing
completedMappings.message: Meaningful connection involves listening, choice and respectful boundaries, not constant closeness or pressure to disclose.

completedMappings.title: Child and Adolescent Mental Health
completedMappings.message: Children and adolescents have different developmental needs; caring adults provide attentive listening and supportive environments.
